items.title: Microsoft AI Event and Fed Minutes Set Stage for Week
points: Microsoft holds Windows and Surface event Wednesday with CEO Satya Nadella and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, emphasizing local AI (AI models running directly on devices without sending data to cloud servers) in Windows.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's attendance signals importance of chip partnerships for Microsoft's local AI strategy.
Fed releases September meeting minutes Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET, with investors focused on inflation, labor market, and future interest rate signals.

items.title: Media Merger Creates Combined Entertainment Giant
points: Paramount-Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery closes Tuesday, combining two major media companies into one entity.
Combined company will operate under the Skydance brand name with ticker symbol SKYD.

items.title: Investor Strategy Amid Market Uncertainty
points: Analysts recommend favoring large technology hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet) over AI chip suppliers due to potential power constraints, financing challenges, and data center delays.

Companies benefiting from potential interest rate declines—housing, transportation, and select REITs (real estate investment trusts, which own and lease properties generating income)—are seen as attractive cyclical plays.
Short-term Treasury ETFs are recommended for cash management, CME Group for volatility exposure, and Canadian Natural Resources for energy positioning.

items.title: Light Earnings Week Ahead
points: PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines, Constellation Brands, and Levi Strauss report earnings this week; Costco releases monthly sales data.

items.title: Micron's Earnings Blow-Out
points: Micron added $43 billion in quarterly sales year-over-year, plus $13 billion sequentially, driven by AI chip demand.
Beat both sales and profit forecasts, with operating margins exceeding 80% in some segments.
Despite strong growth, stock trades at a single-digit forward P/E ratio (price relative to next year's earnings), a rare combination.
Supply constraints are expected to support strong pricing power through 2027-2028, extending the current profitability cycle rather than signaling a cyclical peak.
CEO argues investors are too focused on predicting next quarter's results rather than appreciating the company's current exceptional fundamentals.
Broader lesson: markets often chase the 'next big thing' and undervalue companies already performing exceptionally well in the present.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Micron stock offers an important reminder for investors

headlines: Micron crushed earnings with $43B in quarterly sales growth year-over-year and beat on profit, driven by AI chip demand, yet trades at a single-digit forward P/E ratio (price relative to next year's earnings).
Memory chipmaker signals supply constraints will support strong pricing power through 2028, extending the current profitability cycle.
CEO warns that investors are too focused on predicting the next quarter rather than appreciating Micron's exceptional current fundamentals and 80%+ operating margins in some segments.

sections.title: Micron's Earnings Blow-Out
points: Micron added $43 billion in sales compared to the year-ago quarter, with an additional $13 billion added from the prior quarter alone.
Beat both sales and profit forecasts; operating margins exceeded 80% in some business segments.
Guidance remained strong overall, though margin commentary on the earnings call may have muted market enthusiasm.

sections.title: Why This Valuation Matters
points: Stock trades at a single-digit forward P/E ratio despite growing by billions per quarter—a rare combination across the stock universe.
Supply-demand tightness expected through 2027-2028 will support elevated pricing and earnings, contradicting concerns this represents a cyclical peak.
Investor focus on next quarter's results is causing the market to overlook the strength of current fundamentals and the durability of profitability.

sections.title: The Bigger Lesson
points: Stock markets constantly hunt for the 'next big thing' and often fail to appreciate exceptional current performance, similar to how overachievers constantly chase the next milestone.
Micron's quarter should be evaluated in proper context: the company is executing at an exceptional level right now, not just promising future growth.
